clue.text: Pitcher's filled with craft bitter for dance

indicators.note: to craft something is to shape it skilfully, so the following word is fashioned into a new order
a vessel filled with something holds it inside, so the jug wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a pitcher is a jug
the six letters of bitter rearranged

explanation.surface: A jug brimming with home-brewed bitter beer, kept for a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft bitter' reads as craft beer, but craft is the instruction to rearrange bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: The jitterbug is a lively swing dance popular in the 1940s.

clue.text: Dad supports German agreement with neutral country

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after the first word

parts.note: ja is German for yes
pa is a familiar name for a father
N is the abbreviation for neutral, as on a gear stick or plug

explanation.surface: A father backing a German deal with a neutral nation, a diplomatic scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neutral country' looks like one idea, but neutral only supplies a letter and country alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is an island nation in East Asia, an example of a country.

clue.text: Personal judgment should be following central hypothesis

indicators.note: one piece following another means it is placed after it in the answer
central means only the middle of the following word is kept

parts.note: the two letters at the centre of this ten-letter word
ought and should both express obligation

explanation.surface: A philosopher insisting one's own opinion should follow from a core theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought can mean an opinion or considered view, as in 'my thought is that...'.

clue.text: Patrolled German section of border

indicators.note: a section is a part cut out of something larger, so the letters lie inside the phrase before it

parts.note: found running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Guards patrolled the German stretch of a national frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge of something is its border or outer limit.

clue.text: Strike has a thousand involved in local uprising

indicators.note: rising up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top
to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it

parts.note: a local is a Briton's nearby pub
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A strike action with a thousand people joining a small-town revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local uprising' suggests a regional rebellion; local is the British word for one's regular pub, turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump is to knock or hit against something, so it is a synonym for strike.

clue.text: Greet noisy drunk with kindness

indicators.note: a drunk person's movements are jumbled, so the preceding letters are scrambled

parts.note: both words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Welcoming a loud drunk warmly instead of throwing them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Generosity is liberal giving or goodwill, closely matching kindness.

clue.text: Dog's company put regular grin on Queen!

indicators.note: put on means one piece is placed after another in an across answer

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: regular means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: the first and third letters

explanation.surface: A firm that made a dog grin at the Queen, nodding to the royal pets.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the corgi is the breed famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog.

clue.text: End argument about everybody at party in street in Paris

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the party goes within the street

parts.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
all means everybody
taken as written

explanation.surface: Settling a row among everyone at a street party in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Party is a political party here: C is the usual abbreviation for Conservative, a little loosely clued.
explanation.definitionFit: To call a truce is to agree to stop fighting, so it ends an argument.

clue.text: Phoned about silly nit holding forth

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the call wraps round the other letters

parts.note: rang is the past tense of ring, to phone

indicators.note: something silly is muddled, so the next word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: these three letters reordered

explanation.surface: Someone rang up to lecture a foolish idiot at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranting means speaking at length in a loud, impassioned way, which is holding forth.

clue.text: Having received a legacy, home help's half-embarrassed about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the colour wraps round the following word
only half the word is kept, the other half dropped

parts.note: in means at home
only its first two letters are used
red-faced with embarrassment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaner left money in a will feels a bit awkward about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-embarrassed' looks like one hyphenated idea, but half belongs with help, leaving HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inherited has been passed down as a bequest, so one who inherited received a legacy.

clue.text: All munch nosh-up prepared with good pub food

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made from its ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: all three words supply letters
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Everyone tucking into a feast of decent pub grub.
explanation.walkthrough: A ploughman's lunch is a British pub dish of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: The ploughman's lunch is a classic cold meal served in British pubs.

clue.text: Hitches non-starting horses

indicators.note: a word that does not start has lost its opening letter

parts.note: hitches and snags are both minor problems

explanation.surface: Problems with horses that refuse to leave the starting gate.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-starting horses sounds like a racing complaint, but it tells you to drop a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nags is an informal word for horses, especially old or poor ones.

clue.text: Sadder end in dire neglect

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
something neglected falls into disorder, so the preceding word is jumbled

parts.note: its letters are reordered and split round the other piece
the rear is the back end

explanation.surface: A gloomy end coming in terrible neglect.
explanation.definitionFit: Drearier means more dismal or gloomy, so it is a synonym of sadder.

clue.text: I set up one tying knot, securing circle and lines for sewing

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is raised, so read bottom to top

parts.note: the speaker, I, refers to themself as me

indicators.note: securing means holding firmly within, so the circle goes inside

O is circle-shaped
RY is short for railway lines

explanation.surface: Someone knotting thread, working a circle and lines of stitching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tying knot' reads as a needlework step, but tying the knot is getting married.
explanation.definitionFit: Embroidery is decorative needlework, a form of sewing patterns onto fabric.

clue.text: One fixes pop-up sketch above

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece above comes first

parts.note: a sketch is a drawing

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pop or nip somewhere is to go there briefly

explanation.surface: A pop-up drawing propped on top, like a children's book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop-up' looks like one adjective, but pop is a verb meaning nip and up reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing pin is a thumbtack, the device used to fix paper to a board.

clue.text: Exposes markets' tricks

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them
marts are markets

explanation.surface: An exposé of the dodgy practices of traders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricks' looks like a noun after markets'; it is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsmart someone is to outwit or trick them by cleverness.

clue.text: Tyrant's abuse of poor absorbs newspapers

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so the jumbled letters hold the other piece
abuse mistreats and distorts, so the next word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: its letters are reordered and split around the press
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A dictator's mistreatment of the poor fills the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressor is one who rules cruelly and unjustly, just as a tyrant does.

clue.text: Proper religious ceremony is spoken

indicators.note: spoken means it is the sound of the word that counts, not its spelling

parts.note: a rite is a religious ceremony

explanation.surface: A correct ritual is recited aloud in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Right means correct or appropriate, a synonym of proper.

clue.text: One who's affected by moving prose

indicators.note: moving things around changes their positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: its five letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone emotionally touched by a stirring piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Affected means touched emotionally on the surface, but here it means pretentious.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a person who behaves affectedly to impress others.

clue.text: Puffed up to West Country on old lines with points

parts.note: the West Country is the South West of England
O is short for old
L for line, doubled for the plural
east and north, two compass points

explanation.surface: Travelling to the South West on old railway lines with their points.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is the south-western region of England, abbreviated SW; points are railway switches on the surface but compass points here.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen means enlarged or distended, so it describes something puffed up.

clue.text: Expecting a delivery?

parts.note: surface reading: waiting in for a parcel or the post
setter's reading: expecting a baby to be delivered, i.e. pregnant

explanation.walkthrough: A delivery suggests the postman, but it is also the birth of a baby; expecting is itself a euphemism for pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: With child is an old-fashioned phrase meaning pregnant, someone due to give birth.

clue.text: Island politician with range to make progress

parts.note: I is short for island
a Member of Parliament
to range is to wander or rove

explanation.surface: An island's MP touring widely to get things done.
explanation.walkthrough: Range looks like a noun, as in a mountain range, but it is the verb to roam.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve is to get better, which is making progress.

clue.text: Strong feelings as earth moves

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth, as on electrical wiring
motions are movements

explanation.surface: Passions running high like an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth moves' suggests an anagram of earth; here earth is simply E and moves gives the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotions are intense feelings such as love or anger.

clue.text: See small Post Office at end of street

parts.note: S is short for small
the usual abbreviation

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: Directions: look for a little post office at the bottom of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or catch sight of it, so it means see.

clue.text: Played to young editor

parts.note: taken as written
Y is short for young
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A junior journalist performing for the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to play with it idly, so toyed means played.

clue.text: A prisoner's returning celebration

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: taken as written
an old lag is a habitual prisoner

explanation.surface: A released inmate's homecoming party.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or celebration.

clue.text: Sharp point is said to hurt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the backward-pointing spike on a hook or arrow

explanation.surface: A sharp tip is reputed to be painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' suggests a sound-alike clue, but it belongs to the second meaning: something said in order to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a spiky projection on a hook and a wounding verbal jibe.

clue.text: No clarification required from me on old scheme by a Conservative

parts.note: myself, one's own self
an ex is a former one
a scheme is a plan
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician declining to explain an old Tory plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Something self-explanatory is clear without needing any explanation.

clue.text: Ladder to point unknown is not all solid

parts.note: a ladder in tights, in British usage, is a run
north, a compass point
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A ladder propped against an unknown point is unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladder is the British word for a run in stockings, not something to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Runny means liquid or semi-fluid, so not entirely solid.

clue.text: Old lady's eating a lolly that's served with curry

parts.note: nan is a grandmother
taken as written
both are British slang for money

explanation.walkthrough: Lolly looks like an ice lolly, but it is British slang for money, as is bread.
